slides.title: 5 laundry myths you're probably still falling for

slides.myth: Cold water doesn't get clothes clean.
slides.fact: With a cold-water detergent, cold does fine on most loads. Heating the water is about 90% of the energy a load uses. Oily stains are the exception.
slides.source: ENERGY STAR and U.S. Department of Energy

slides.fact: Extra detergent doesn't clean better. It leaves residue on your clothes and buildup in the machine, and too many suds cushion clothes so they rub less.

slides.myth: A little lint in the dryer is harmless.
slides.fact: Federal estimates count about 15,500 dryer fires a year, and not cleaning is the leading cause. Empty the lint filter every load.
slides.source: U.S. CPSC and U.S. Fire Administration

slides.myth: A "Dry Clean" tag means you can never wash it.
slides.fact: Under the FTC rule a label only has to list one safe method. "Dry Clean Only" is the warning that washing will damage it. Plain "Dry Clean" isn't.
slides.source: Federal Trade Commission, Care Labeling Rule

slides.myth: Stuffing the washer full saves time.
slides.fact: Clothes that can't tumble don't rub clean, and the detergent may not dissolve well. Leave room for the load to move, about 80% full.
